## What I do

I design and build web applications, mobile applications, e-commerce platforms, and AI systems. I take responsibility for the whole product — not just one layer of it. Every project is delivered with:

- Modern design — clear interfaces, current craft, no decoration for its own sake.
- SEO structured from the first line — not added later as a patch.
- Secure handling of data, authentication, and third-party integrations.
- Fast hosting and deployment — infrastructure chosen for speed and stability.
- Responsive layouts — the site adapts to phone, tablet, or desk.

Server architecture, microservices and REST APIs in Python (FastAPI, Django REST Framework), PostgreSQL modelling, queues with Celery and Redis, WebSocket message buses, React/Next.js/Vue interfaces, Playwright automation, and a pool of Linux VPS machines in Docker.

- **5+ years** of continuous commercial practice.

## Engineering stack

- **Backend & API** — Python, FastAPI, Django REST Framework, Django Ninja, AsyncIO, REST, WebSockets, Celery, Redis.
- **Frontend** — JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js 15 (App Router, SSR/SSG), Zustand, Redux Toolkit, Tailwind CSS, next-intl.
- **Databases** — PostgreSQL (relational schema design, composite B-tree/GIN indexes, EXPLAIN ANALYZE tuning, JSONB), Redis (caching, pub/sub).
- **DevOps & infrastructure** — Linux VPS (Ubuntu/Debian), Docker & Docker Compose, Nginx reverse proxy, SSL/Certbot, PM2, Bash automation, Git, CI/CD.

## Services

- Full-stack web development — complete products built from the ground up.
- Frontend development with React and Next.js — responsive interfaces, animation, complex client-side interactions.
- Backend development with Django — REST APIs, authentication, business logic, database-driven systems.
- E-commerce, booking systems, dashboards, CRMs, SaaS products, and custom business applications.
- Third-party integrations — payments, messaging, external APIs, authentication providers, analytics.
- Deployment and production setup — servers, databases, domains, SSL, monitoring, and maintenance.

## Pricing approach

Every project is different, so I estimate from the actual brief rather than selling artificial packages. Small fixes, integrations, and individual features can be handled as focused tasks. Larger products are planned in stages so that the client always understands what is being built and why. The goal is not the cheapest possible version — it is something that can actually be used, maintained, and developed further.

## Technology stack

HTML, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript, React, Next.js, Django, Python, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Node.js, REST APIs, auth, integrations, deployment and DevOps.

## Why clients work with me

- I take ownership — when I accept a project, I get it to a usable result.
- I think beyond the screen — data, architecture, logic, integrations, performance, deployment, maintenance.
- I finish what I start — requirements change and problems appear; the responsibility stays the same.
- I keep client work confidential — a significant part of professional development happens under NDA.

## FAQ (short answers)

1. **Can you build a project from scratch?** Yes. Start with an idea, specification, prototype, design, or existing business process; I help translate it into a technical architecture and build through to deployment.
2. **Can you work with an existing design?** Yes. I turn it into a responsive production interface and connect it to the backend and required services, flagging technical issues in the design early.
3. **Do you only work on the frontend?** No. My focus is full-stack: React and Next.js on the frontend, Django and PostgreSQL on the backend, plus APIs, authentication, integrations, and deployment.
4. **What if I don't have a technical specification?** That is fine. Most projects start as a business idea and a conversation; I help break the idea into features and an actionable plan.
5. **Do you work under NDA?** Yes. Confidentiality is a normal part of professional software development, and I treat it as the default for client work.
6. **What about sensitive or private data?** Sensitive information is handled carefully from the beginning: access control, authentication, secrets, permissions, and third-party services are part of the architecture, not afterthoughts.
7. **Will you leave after the website goes live?** Not necessarily. Launch is a milestone. If you need fixes, improvements, new functionality, or continued technical support, we continue working together.
8. **What if something goes wrong during development?** Something unexpected eventually happens in almost every non-trivial project. I communicate the problem clearly, explain the options, and work toward a practical solution.
